question.worked_solution:
To find the GCF, we list the factors of the coefficients and identify any common variable factors in the expressions.

The factors of $12$ are

$$
1,\,2,\,3,\,4,\,6,\,12.
$$

The factors of $18$ are

$$
1,\,2,\,3,\,6,\,9,\,18.
$$

The factors of $30$ are

$$
1,\,2,\,3,\,5,\,6,\,10,\,15,\,30.
$$

The common factors of $12,$ $18,$ and $30$ are

$$
1,\,2,\,3,\,6.
$$

The greatest of these common factors is $6.$

Now we look at the variable factors. The expressions $12z,$ $18z,$ and $30z$ all contain $z.$

Thus, the $\text{GCF}$ of $12z,$ $18z,$ and $30z$ is $6z.$
